full_judgment: The opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 141 of 1985 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in the suit land. The suit was ultimately decreed ex-parte on 9.11.85. Thereafter the defendant petitioner filed two applications and the said applications were registered as Miscellaneous Case Nos. 4 of 1986 and 12 of 1986 and the said Miscellaneous Cases were heard analogously and dismissed by the trial Court on 20.12.88 Thereafter the defendant petitioner preferred 2 Miscellaneous Appeals in this cowl being Miscellaneous Appeals Nos. 336 of 1988 and 17 of 1989. During pendency of the Miscellaneous Appeals in this court, the original plaintiff respondent No. 2 died on 20.3.90. On an application, filed by the defendant petitioner, the heirs of plaintiff respondent No.2 were substituted in these appeals on 5.1.91. Both the appeals were taken up for hearing analogously and this court by its order dated 5.1.91 allowed the appeals and set aside the ex-parte decree dated 9.11.85. The order of this court was communicated and the L.C. Records were sent down to the trial court and the same were received by the trial court on 25.3.90. Thereafter the heirs of the original plaintiff No. 2 filed an application under order 1 Rule 10 for adding them as plaintiffs in the suit. The suit was originally instituted by 2 plaintiffs, namely plaintiff No. 1 Abdul Karim and plaintiff No.2 Sohala Khatun wife of plaintiff No.1. On the death Sohala Khatun plaintiff No.2, her husband, her sons and others became her heirs and successors-in-interest in respect of the property. On the application filed by the heirs of decesed plaintiff No.2 the trial court allowed the application after hearing of the par ties on 39490 In the meantime the heirs of the de plaintiff No. 2 filed a application for substituting them as decree-holder in the execution case on 18.6.89. But no action could be taken on the application for substitution of the heirs of the deceased plaintiff No.2 as decree holder as stay was granted by: this court in the aforesaid Miscellaneous appeals.
